stresses: EXTERNAL VALIDATION TARGET #2, named after target #1 (fastify) closed as NOT_QUALIFIED, and before the repository was cloned or any date-fns DiffCI data existed (docs/external-target-02-selection.md). pnpm monorepo, workspace pkgs/* (core, tz, utc, docs, dev), vitest 4. testCommandRationale: The root package.json has NO scripts block at all - CI drives tests through mise tasks - so there is no root script to select. The root ships its own vitest.config.ts declaring projects: [pkgs/*], and bare `vitest run` against it is the repository own declaration of its test surface. This is the identical uniform non-interactive invocation applied to hono. No project filter, exclusion, or include glob was invented: each package own committed config decides its file set. Narrowing to pkgs/core alone was considered and REJECTED - it would pre-screen the repository into a friendlier shape, which is a form of tuning. Checked in advance because the validation contract forbids launching a browser: pkgs/core/vitest.config.ts imports @vitest/browser-playwright but leaves the browser instance commented out (enabled only by the separate test/browser task via --browser), so `vitest run` runs in node.
buildRationale: No build. pkgs/core exports map points at ./src/index.ts, so workspace consumers (tz, utc, docs) resolve TypeScript source and vitest transpiles it - the same situation as vue, where a build would have been required only if tests imported package outputs.

economicsEvidence: immer-economics-01 (2026-08-30, canonical Linux, agent B): incrementalCpu = 79.51 - (21.61 + 10.93) = +46.97 CPU-s; grossCpu = +46.48. 7 of 7 compute-measurable candidates individually positive. OUT-OF-SAMPLE TEST: the POSITIVE sign was frozen at bae2d00 before this run existed and was CORRECT - the eligibility rule's first out-of-sample sign match. MAGNITUDE WRONG: the frozen prediction was +129.67 over 25 observations while economics covered only 7 candidates; restricted post-hoc to those 7 the rule predicts +85.19 against +46.97 measured, a 1.8x over-prediction. Cause measured, not assumed: the DiffCI arm cost 21.61 CPU-s for 8 files (~2.7 CPU-s/file) against a modelled 0.6539, because vitest's fixed startup cost dominates at 1-2 file selections. The error direction INFLATES predicted savings. The comparator selected 22-23 of 23 files on every candidate and cost 79.51 against 79.02 for running everything - worse than no selection at all - so DiffCI's win here owes at least as much to the comparator's failure as to its own precision.
